title: Embed templates, static files and migrations in the binary
description: The app finds migrations/, templates/ and static/ relative to the current working directory (main.go:28-33, 226-240) and the compose file bind-mounts templates and static over the image copies. Embed all three with go:embed so the binary is self-contained, keeping a development mode that reads from disk for live editing (the existing TEMPLATE_RELOAD behaviour). golang-migrate reads migrations through its iofs source. Uploaded club logos (WI-119) live on the data volume, outside the embedded tree. Also vendor htmx into static/ (it is loaded from unpkg in 30 places and jsdelivr in 2) so an instance has no third-party script dependency.

recommended_model.name: Opus 5.5
recommended_model.rationale: Changes how every template and asset is located; moderate blast radius.

acceptance_criteria: The binary runs from any directory with only a data directory beside it
Development mode still picks up template and static edits without a rebuild
Migrations run from the embedded source; cmd/migrate and cmd/migrate-down become subcommands of the main binary or use the same embedded source
No page loads script or style from a third-party host
The production compose file no longer bind-mounts templates or static
Static assets are served with sensible cache headers and a version-based cache-buster

files_to_create: embed.go at module root (or assets package)
notes: go:embed cannot reach parent directories - the embedding file must sit at or above templates/, static/ and migrations/.
Keep htmx at the version in use (1.9.4) unless an upgrade is tested.

testing_requirements: Run the binary from an empty temp directory in a scratch container

context.user_story: As a club operator, I want one file (or one image) to run, with nothing else to keep in sync.
context.programme: Club-readiness programme (sprints 019-024). Agreed constraints: BHPLTA clubs only; each club self-hosts its own instance; the original author must have no access to any other club's instance (no seeded accounts, no shared or default secrets, no phone-home); passkeys are the default sign-in with passwords as an optional fallback; the captain role is real; SQLite is the only supported database; CourtHive is bundled as an opt-in part of the package so clubs can run their own club championships.
